outcome: No proof, disproof, partial result, or bound on Jacobson's conjecture (that the intersection of all powers of the Jacobson radical of a two-sided Noetherian ring is zero) was found dated after 26 January 2024. All substantive results located predate the window (Herstein's 1965 counterexample for one-sided Noetherian rings, Jategaonkar's second-layer-condition work, Lenagan's Krull-dimension-one case, Cauchon/Cauchon-type fully-bounded-Noetherian results). The conjecture remains open in general for two-sided Noetherian rings.
summary: I independently re-ran and extended the triage's search, confirming its 'none' verdict. Searches for the conjecture's exact name, for 'intersection of powers of the Jacobson radical' plus 'Noetherian', for arXiv listings, and for any AI/machine-learning involvement all returned either (a) pre-2024 classical results — Herstein's 1965 counterexample for one-sided Noetherian rings, Jategaonkar's work, the fully-bounded-Noetherian and Krull-dimension-one special cases, all dated to the 1970s-2010s — or (b) unrelated hits on similarly named but distinct objects: the Jacobian conjecture (polynomial maps with polynomial inverses, which did see a 2026 AI-assisted counterexample per a UTEP tech report, arxiv 2311.14723-adjacent discussion, and other Jacobian-conjecture papers — a completely different problem), 'Jacobson rings' in the commutative-algebra/Nullstellensatz sense (Stacks project, Emerton notes), 'left Jacobson rings' (arXiv:2503.16005, a 2025 paper I opened directly and confirmed defines an unrelated one-sided Nullstellensatz-style property, not the radical-power conjecture), and Jacobson's ring-commutativity theorem (x^n=x). I checked the Wikipedia article on Jacobson's conjecture itself (still describes it as open, most recent citation 1982) and the Grokipedia mirror (same conclusion, no post-2024 developments, no AI mention). No survey, preprint, or announcement anywhere in these searches claims new movement on this specific conjecture since 26 January 2024. This agrees with the triage's verdict; I found nothing it missed.
competing_reading: None found. The only genuine ambiguity is nomenclature: several unrelated objects share 'Jacobson' in their name (Jacobian conjecture, Jacobson rings, left Jacobson rings, Jacobson's commutativity theorem), and a careless search could misattribute the Jacobian conjecture's 2026 AI-assisted counterexample to this problem. I verified each of these is a distinct mathematical object from Jacobson's conjecture on the radical, so none of it counts as a case or variant of the stated problem — it is out of scope entirely under §3.1, not merely a related problem.
what_would_settle_it: A dated preprint or journal paper explicitly addressing the intersection of powers of the Jacobson radical for general (or a new special class of) two-sided Noetherian rings, submitted after 26 January 2024 — none was found in this search.
